paper_metadata.title: Effects of alloying elements on microstructure and mechanical properties of Co–Ni–Al–Ti superalloy

evidence.quote: The effects of the relative content of Al and Ti, and the addition of 2 at.% Cr or Mo to substitute partly Co on the microstructure and mechanical properties of Co-Ni-Al-Ti superalloy were investigated.

Five superalloys were produced by arc melting from pure metals of at least 99.9% purity under an argon atmosphere. Each ingot was inverted and remelted 6 times to ensure homogeneity
The cast superalloys were homogenized at 1473 K for 24 h and followed by water cooling to minimize the effect of segregation
the homogenized superalloys were subjected to aging treatment at 923 K for 20 h, 100 h and 200 h, and followed by air cooling to attain the stable microstructure

evidence.quote: the inter-dendritic region was γ'-(Co, Ni) 3(Al, Ti) phase and the dendrite region was γ-Co matrix phase

evidence.section: 3.2 Microstructures of the as-cast and aged superalloys
evidence.quote: The five as-cast alloys exhibited similar microstructures, showing a dendritic structure with certain directionality, and cuboidal phases with non-uniform sizes and shapes continuously distributed in the inter-dendritic regions

evidence.section: 3.2 Microstructures of the as-cast and aged superalloys
